**Finding: compliant — no redline proposed.**

Section 18 (§ 18.1–18.2) is the document's only insurance provision, and it runs against Brightline as Vendor — i.e., it benefits us as Customer. It satisfies every element of the **preferred** position:

| Preferred element | Status |
|---|---|
| CGL ≥ USD 1M / occurrence | ✓ § 18.1 |
| CGL ≥ USD 2M aggregate | ✓ § 18.1 |
| E&O ≥ USD 2M | ✓ § 18.1 |
| Cyber/privacy ≥ USD 5M where Customer Data processed | ✓ § 18.1 (unconditional — broader than required) |
| Workers' comp as required by law | ✓ § 18.1 |
| Certificates on request | ✓ § 18.2 |

Additional Vendor-favourable-to-us terms beyond the playbook ask: a one-year tail after the term, employer's liability of USD 1M, reputable insurers, primary cover where commercially customary, advance notice of cancellation or material reduction, and an express statement that insurance does not limit Vendor's liabilities.

Diligence on dilution: I confirmed party direction from the preamble (Northwind = Customer, Brightline = Vendor), cross-checked § 17 (Information Security) per the planner hint to confirm Vendor does process Customer Data so the cyber cover is genuinely engaged, reviewed the full section list for any schedule or side provision on insurance, and ran targeted searches for self-insurance, retentions, "commercially available" qualifiers, and any "notwithstanding Section 18" override. Nothing responsive — § 18 stands unqualified.

Since the clause sits at preferred rather than merely fallback, there is no basis to redline, and I have not proposed one.
